measures actual suite consumption.

Under a
$0 upfront provider-owned model
, the service provider supplies and maintains the equipment under a long-term agreement. Axis Meter Solutions describes a standard

Tenant Billing Reporting and Maintenance Through the Agreement

Once the meters go live, the property needs more than a monthly invoice file. The operating layer should turn reads into resident charges, exception reports, owner dashboards, and documented service actions.

A sound workflow captures the read, checks it against the account and prior consumption pattern, applies the permitted billing rules, and produces an invoice that residents can understand. Property staff should be able to see whether a charge came from an actual read or an estimate, which suites have unresolved exceptions, and whether a move-in or move-out date affected the billing period.

Residents need clarity:
Meter read dates, billing periods, rate information, and support contacts.
Managers need action lists:
Missing reads, abnormal flow, access issues, disputed invoices, and service tickets.
Owners need operating control:
Recoveries, arrears, consumption by building area, common-area demand, and unresolved exceptions.

A provider-owned model is only useful if those obligations are written into the service scope rather than left to informal promises.

Ask who owns the raw data and how quickly you can export it if management changes. Confirm whether reports can be consolidated across a portfolio, whether suites can be added without redesigning the whole platform, and how the provider handles tenant privacy. Do not accept an annual benefit figure unless the provider shows its assumptions. Pressure-test the baseline billing method, suite access, tenant mix, common-area allocation, likely leak-response process, agreement fees, and exit terms. The federal data gap matters here. Canada's main residential indicator runs through 2011, so current behavioural and savings assumptions need to come from your property's own billing and consumption records rather than a national headline. (Canada's open residential water-use dataset)

Before signing, verify:

  • Billing authority: Lease, condominium, municipal, and provincial requirements.
  • Meter compliance: Approval, commissioning, and replacement standards.
  • Commercial terms: Agreement length, ownership, termination, and transfer rights.
  • Operating scope: Billing, collections support, alerts, maintenance, and reporting.
  • Implementation commitments: Access plan, notices, permits, testing, and go-live controls.
